**Answer** | Item | Detail | |------|--------| | **First Studio Ghibli film to win the Japan Academy Film Prize – Picture of the Year** | *Princess Mononoke* (released in Japan in 1997). It captured the top honor at the 21st Japan Academy Film Prize ceremony held in February 1998. | | **Key source(s)** | • Official “Japan Academy Prize” archive lists *Princess Mononoke* as the 1998 Picture‑of‑the‑Year recipient.
• Major Japanese newspapers (e.g., *Asahi Shimbun*, *Yomiuri Shimbun*) reported the award immediately afterward.
• International press coverage (e.g., *Variety*, *Hollywood Reporter*) highlighted the significance of a domestic animation title sweeping the country’s most prestigious film award. | --- ### How the Box‑Office Success Influenced Global Popularity | Aspect | Impact | |-------|--------| | **Domestic Gross** | *Princess Mononoke* earned ¥12.5 billion (~US$120 million) in Japan alone—making it the highest‑grossing animated feature there up to that point. This record‑breaking performance proved that anime could command blockbuster status beyond niche markets. | | **International Distribution** | The movie opened in North America (via Disney/Touchstone Pictures) in late 1998, earning roughly US$30 million worldwide outside Japan. Its commercial viability convinced major distributors to acquire rights to future Ghibli titles. | | **Critical Acclaim & Word‑Of‑Mouth** | Winning Picture of the Year gave the film instant credibility among mainstream audiences who typically favored live‑action dramas. Critics praised its storytelling depth, environmental themes, and cinematic artistry, prompting broader media attention across Europe, Latin America, and Asia. | | **Catalyst for Subsequent Releases** | After seeing the global appetite for *Princess Mononoke*, studios began investing heavily in subtitling/dubbing infrastructure, marketing budgets, and localized releases for later Ghibli works (*Howl’s Moving Castle*, *Kiki’s Delivery Service*, *Spirited Away*). | | **Cultural Exchange & Anime Boom** | The film’s success accelerated the “anime boom” of the late ’90s and early 2000s. Western broadcasters added Ghibli content to their lineups, while streaming platforms later secured exclusive licenses, further expanding the fanbase. | | **Legacy & Brand Strengthening** | By proving itself both critically acclaimed and commercially viable, *Princess Mononoke* cemented Studio Ghibli’s reputation as a world‑class filmmaker. That brand equity made subsequent titles easier to market abroad, turning each new release into a highly anticipated event rather than a risky venture. | #### Bottom Line Winning the Japan Academy Film Prize for Picture of the Year marked a watershed moment for Studio Ghibli. Coupled with unprecedented domestic earnings, *Princess Mononoke* demonstrated that high‑quality animation could dominate mainstream cinema—a realization that spurred aggressive international expansion, broadened audience demographics, and laid the groundwork for Ghibli’s enduring global legacy.
